# CPDataKit v0.9.0

2026-09-20

CPDataKit v0.9.0 makes the local workbench easier to use and strengthens numeric fidelity
and recovery when processing scientific data.

## Workbench and reports

- A Chinese workbench organizes preparation, validation and results into clear steps. The
  selected file and schema stay visible; validation results retain the selection they checked.
- Advanced schema drafting, mapping previews and multidimensional slices remain available in
  expandable sections. Output conflicts identify the path and require an explicit overwrite choice.
- Completed tasks link to their registered artifacts. Pending result saves remain distinguishable
  from durable completion, while historical resource lists load on demand.
- Offline HTML reports show validation summaries, statistics tables and readable provenance.
  Full metadata remains available in expandable details. JSON and Markdown contracts are preserved.

## Data integrity and recovery

- Preserve exact integer values and scalar categories through supported conversions, and reject
  representations that cannot preserve the values. Standard unit declarations and coordinate units
  are resolved consistently; conflicting declarations remain validation errors.
- Keep integer extrema exact and stabilize finite numeric summaries. Unrepresentable comparison
  deltas carry an explicit reason instead of silently overflowing or losing integer precision.
- Save independent job-completion evidence, retry catalog persistence, and replay verified results
  on restart. An operating-system lock prevents two workbenches from writing the same workspace.
- Record interrupted output transactions and expose a recovery inventory. Recovery checks file
  identity, ownership and hashes, then copies verified content to an unoccupied destination.
- Harden upload rollback, preserve existing outputs during concurrent changes, and avoid redundant
  Zarr directory scans. The local UI no longer requires the development-only httpx package.

## Compatibility and scope

Python 3.12 or newer is required. Existing public Python/CLI interfaces, schema 1.0 and 2.0,
and CPDataKit HDF5 1.0 and 2.0 remain supported. User-facing workbench and HTML report text is now
primarily Chinese; field names, units and scientific definitions retain their original declarations.

Recovery covers the tested process-interruption cases, not arbitrary power loss. Heatmap output
uses its existing publication path. If both catalog storage and independent completion evidence
cannot be persisted, results cannot be guaranteed after process exit. Some nullable/object values
remain unsupported by specific storage backends and are rejected explicitly.

The documented CF-time selective-read boundary remains: for nonmonotonic axes with hidden interior
out-of-range dates, use full loading followed by `isel` when exact full-axis type inference matters.
Validation checks declared data rules; it does not establish physical equivalence or experimental validity.

## Get started

```bash
python -m pip install --upgrade "cpdatakit==0.9.0"
cpdatakit ui
```

See the [workbench guide](https://github.com/koocmitwho/cpdatakit/blob/v0.9.0/docs/workbench-guide.md)
and [quickstart](https://github.com/koocmitwho/cpdatakit/blob/v0.9.0/docs/quickstart.md).
Implementation evidence is recorded in the
[fidelity/recovery verification](https://github.com/koocmitwho/cpdatakit/blob/v0.9.0/docs/verification/2026-09-19-fidelity-recovery.md)
and [UI verification](https://github.com/koocmitwho/cpdatakit/blob/v0.9.0/docs/verification/2026-09-20-ui-readability.md).
Release checks are recorded on the release pull request and its GitHub Actions runs.
